evidence.quote: Each player antes 10, so the pot is 20 and your bankroll starts at 1,000 minus the ante.
The dealer's king-high hand (K-10-9-8-6) beats your queen-high hand (Q-J-9-7-5)

criteria.why: The replies are mostly plain dealer talk with no JSON or tool talk. A few lines read like analysis, such as the bankroll arithmetic, and the Turn 1 "you act first" is slightly wordy, so one small slip.

evidence.quote: You checked. The dealer checked too, so the hand moves to fourth street.
The hand is over: the dealer's king-high beat your queen-high

criteria.why: Each reply acts on the check, and on the final turn it says the hand is over and offers another hand or a new game. The Turn 6 click found no button and no agent turn ran, so there is no reply to judge there.

evidence.quote: seventh street was dealt: you drew the 2 of hearts and the dealer drew the 10 of diamonds
so the dealer takes the 20 pot

criteria.why: The Croupier deals every street, reveals the hidden cards at showdown and settles the pot itself. It makes no choices for the player beyond the check the player requested.

evidence.quote: The dealer's king-high hand (K-10-9-8-6) beats your queen-high hand (Q-J-9-7-5)

criteria.why: The reply and surface agree on the winner, the pot and the bankroll of 990. The Turn 4 surface cards are 7, 9, Q, J, 3, 5, 2 against 4, K, 6, 2, 9, 8, 10, so the claimed best-five hands are questionable, since the dealer has a pair of nines and the player a pair of twos. Calling both hands high-card looks wrong and the dealer would still win, so this is a few slips the player would shrug off.
